summary: Dynamic EIP reuse by customer egress NAT causing TLS session misassociation and selective 403s on presigned artifact ranges
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on AtlasHealth private deployment observe intermittent 403s and failed range downloads when fetching model shard blobs via presigned URLs. Failures are selective (some range requests on the same presigned URL succeed while others immediately return 403).

Impact:
- Production inference latency spikes for AtlasHealth (enterprise), degraded tail latency and occasional model load failures causing short application errors.
- Affects a subset of serving nodes and only for requests routed through AtlasHealth corporate egress appliance cluster.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC peering to Redwood control plane), customer-managed egress (NAT+proxy) with dynamic Elastic IPs on egress fleet.
- prod-us-east-1, serving nodes in us-east-1a/b.
- Observed primarily against model gptx-7b-v1 artifact fetches and subsequent tokenization stage.

Observed symptoms / Logs:
- Proxy logs show reuse of outbound source IPs (EIPs) across different client endpoints with short-lived 4-tuple collisions.
- Redwood artifact service logs: several 403 responses logged for presigned range GETs with x-amz-request-id present. Subsequent identical range GETs (replayed) often succeed.
- Serving node side: grpc stream reconnects, KV-cache rehydration stalls for affected shards.
- Customer reported spikes at ~22:15-23:45 UTC on 2026-03-09 with correlated increase in 403 counts and inference latencies.

Initial hypothesis:
- The customer's egress NAT reuses source ports and EIPs aggressively; presigned URLs include ephemeral headers/signatures that rely on client IP path affinity for multi-range downloads or signed headers that the egress appliance mutates when reusing pooled connections. This leads to signature mismatches or request attribution confusion on S3-presigned backend, producing selective 403s for range segments.

Steps to reproduce (attempted by Support):
1) From a host behind a NAT that rotates EIPs, request a presigned multipart/range download for a large model shard.
2) Rapidly issue parallel range requests from different local ports and observe responses.
3) Capture tcpdump on egress to observe source port/EIP reuse and compare to server-side logs.

Evidence attached (logs snippets pasted below):
- Proxy tcpdump: repeated source-port reuse after NAT pool exhaustion (timestamped).
- Artifact service 403 lines: "403 SignatureDoesNotMatch x-amz-request-id: ABC123" for range bytes 0-1048575 then 200 for 1048576-2097151.

Business urgency:
- Enterprise customer, causing degraded production inference; P1 severity, customer requested expedited investigation and mitigation guidance.
steps_to_reproduce: From behind an egress NAT that dynamically rotates public EIPs, request a large presigned artifact and issue multiple parallel range GETs
Observe TCP 4-tuples (src ip, src port, dst ip, dst port) for collisions or reuse
Correlate failed range requests with NAT translation events in customer egress logs
investigation_notes: 03/10 09:20 - Support confirmed 403 spikes correlate to times when customer egress autoscaler cycled nat instances
03/10 12:05 - Captured packet traces show multiple local connections mapping to the same external (EIP,port) within seconds after NAT pool refill
03/11 02:30 - Reproduced selective 403 locally by simulating EIP rotation with an iptables SNAT cluster and multi-range requests
comments: Priya Rao (Support): Raised with customer and requested full proxy config + NAT translation logs.
AtlasHealth network team (via email): Confirmed they run a pool of NAT appliances with dynamic EIP assignment and aggressive port reuse settings to conserve 16k ephemeral ports.
Liam Chen (SRE): Reproduced locally and opened infra PR to add better logging of x-forwarded-for + tls-session-id correlation for artifact requests: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/624
Liam Chen (SRE): Temporary mitigation suggested to customer - pin egress EIP per node and increase ephemeral port pool; customer to test at 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC
root_cause: Customer egress NAT pool reassigns Elastic IPs and aggressively reuses source ports across short time windows. This causes presigned range requests to be attributed inconsistently at the storage endpoint (signature/host/path binding assumptions), resulting in selective 403s and subsequent serving node cache stalls.
resolution: Workaround implemented and validated: AtlasHealth pinned Elastic IPs for their NAT instances used by serving nodes and increased ephemeral port allocation. After changes, 403 rate dropped to baseline and inference tail latency normalized.\nLonger-term: recommend customer adopt per-node EIP stickiness for artifact fetch path or implement connection pinning on their egress proxy. Redwood SRE to add correlation logging (tls session id + x-forwarded-for) to make similar investigations faster. PR #624 added enhanced logging and a flag to detect inconsistent source attribution.
follow_up_actions: SRE: Merge PR #624 and deploy enhanced artifact request attribution logs (ETA 2026-03-15)
Support: Draft KB article for customers on 'Egress NAT port management and presigned URL pitfalls' (owner: Priya Rao)
Customer: Tested and confirmed fix on 2026-03-12, consider gradual rollback to dynamic EIP only after monitoring window
resolution_status: Workaround implemented; monitoring for 72h post-change. Awaiting closure when customer confirms stable (expected by 2026-03-15).
